status: Initial core settings preparation completed and verified; full R7/R8 goal remains active

implementation.startup: main/index awaits one private initializeSettings owner before identity, plugins, IPC and window creation. Existing synchronous loadSettings API is retained for compatibility.
implementation.worker: Async settings-file IO feeds the existing bounded settings worker. Pure shared normalization, parsing and full canonical JSON run there; main receives the owned cache and text. Worker base is reused by later encoding.
implementation.extensions: Main-owned registered-section defaults/normalizers retain callback order and property-key toJSON semantics. Extension fields alone are recanonicalized; registration changes retry at most eight times.
implementation.lifecycle: Profile/generation checks reject late owners; sync compatibility reads/writes supersede pending startup. Debounced encoding waits for startup. Graceful/forced disposal prevents worker resurrection.
implementation.recovery: Async primary and backup validation preserves explicit restore, future-version refusal, exact legacy bytes and corrupt originals. Read generation and bytes are checked again before adoption. Private parse fragments are masked.
implementation.publicApi: initializeSettings and recoverSettingsBackup remain hidden from the plugin settings facade. Renderer settings still use the separate redacting reader; public result shapes are unchanged.

nodeCases: coalesced startup publishes one detached canonical cache, preserves private/extension data and special keys, and remains read-only
10000-tag initial preparation performs zero full main JSON.parse, synchronous settings reads and synchronous canonical-path calls; captured previous source is a positive control when present
a synchronous reader/write during startup supersedes the old storage read and its newer cache cannot be overwritten
a debounced synchronous save waits for an actually blocked startup worker, then durably commits the newer intent without a busy-serializer failure
late extension registration retries the owned read, keeps main-owned callback/toJSON semantics and hides startup privileges from the plugin facade
changed profile scopes and shutdown invalidate late preparation, without publishing an old profile or reviving a closed worker
storage generation and byte revalidation reject superseded/external edits, while later backups retain exact previous committed bytes
asynchronous startup keeps explicit backup consent, corrupt originals, future-version refusal and read-only missing-profile behavior
startup worker masks private parser fragments, enforces configured size limits, hands its canonical base to later encoding and closes without a shutdown dialog
startup crash, malformed reply, timeout and worker construction failure settle callers, retire owned workers and permit recovery

regressions.shutdownPersistence: durable final progress, repeated quit and bounded stuck cleanup passed after final settings change

asar.scope: Actual Electron preparation and subsequent encode from a dedicated minimal ASAR, including all relative worker/normalizer/schema imports. No native window, full installer or interactive startup timing.

verification.ci: Local script mapping and YAML parsed; cloud CI not executed.
verification.conditions: Actual Node workers/storage in isolated VM owners; controlled delay/fault cases. Minimal Electron ASAR exercises the real worker module tree. Complete source main/index, preload, IPC and existing production dist run in a separate Chinese/space profile with 10000 generated tag keys and an empty library; native window was hidden except showInactive capture, never always-on-top. Hardware acceleration disabled for this smoke test. No real video decode or native performance budget acceptance.

limits: Only initial core settings preparation moved off-main. Later plugin registration can still normalize/clone the entire cache; plugin and other legacy loadSettings consumers remain synchronous.
Large extension callbacks execute in their main-thread owner. Worker messages still structured-clone values; renderer JSON/contract preparation is separate.
This does not establish total application startup latency or the original two-second interaction gate. The explicitly requested splash remains a 2.5-second presentation.
Worker timeout and generation checks bound owned work and reject stale publication; an OS filesystem call in a worker is not a promise of immediate physical cancellation.
The unchanged R6 Windows bundle predates this stage. Prior 20-minute native results apply to that frozen bundle and are not reattributed to current startup source.
Physical Android 60-minute PSS/FPS/LAN, other Windows/media matrices, iOS, signing/identity migration and historical theme drift remain open.
retainedFailures: The first evidence finalizer stopped after preservation checks because the local yaml module is absent. It was corrected to use the already installed js-yaml module; no application test or production source failed in that step.
